# About
You can call me a half-vegetation and half-(meta)community ecologist.

I am a latina from **Brazil**, so if you like we can talk in *Portuguese*!
I consider myself fluent in English (but I am always trying to improve) and a beginner*ish* in French (we can give it a try!).

I got my **BSc in Biology** (2021) and **MSc in EcoEvoBio** (2024) from Universidade Estadual Paulista (UNESP), in Rio Claro, Brazil. Where I also worked as research technian for a year (2025) with data management of the [Cerrado On Fire](https://bv.fapesp.br/pt/bolsas/224767/implementacao-de-um-banco-de-dados-sobre-dados-ecologicos-de-comunidades-de-plantas-sob-manejo-de-fo/) project.

I started working on disturbance ecology during my BSc, when I [studied](https://repositorio.unesp.br/server/api/core/bitstreams/8201fbe9-6338-4035-9833-f5ffc20c051f/content) changes in beta diversity across communities under different fire regimes. Later in my BSc, I also explored the combined effects of biological invasion and fire on plant communities, which resulted in [my first publication](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jvs.13250).

Over the years, my interest in vegetation ecology kept growing, especially through my work with the herbaceous-shrub layer of the Cerrado, which I still consider the most beautiful biome in the world. But more recently, my interests have expanded beyond fire itself. This shift led me to pursue a PhD with a more macroecological perspective, where I now focus on the **ecological mechanisms** and not on a specific disturbance.

My current research focuses on how novel disturbance regimes affect different components of biodiversity across temporal, spatial, and organizational scales. While my work is often grounded in fire-driven ecosystems, I am also interested in other types of disturbances, such as **drought** and **herbivory**, and in how these processes shape **open ecosystems** and plant communities more generally.

I’m really into **open science, good data practices**, and all the conversations around making **research better and more accessible**. I could happily spend a long time talking about FAIR principles and related topics. These interests have also led me to think more broadly about the *kind of academic culture we build*, which is why I’ve been spending more of my recent time engaging with questions around equity and mental well-being in academia.

If you are interested in discussing or collaborating on any of these topics, feel free to get in touch.
